evals.name: full-report-purchasing-power
evals.prompt: Build me a core ETF portfolio for the USD 200k. I'm already retired, not taking withdrawals, and the goal is keeping purchasing power over the long run. Full report I can save.
evals.expected_output: Seven-section report. Must treat this as a real-return mandate (inflation-linked exposure considered on merit, not as an afterthought), state expected USD real return against US CPI with no BRL translation or IPCA comparison, propose a rebalancing policy based on bands and top-ups rather than a calendar, size sleeves against USD 200k, and avoid any specific Brazilian tax rates. Date-stamped tables, n/v for unverified fields, real source URLs.

evals.name: casual-two-fund-comparison
evals.prompt: quick one - is VWCE better than VT for me? i keep going back and forth on this
evals.expected_output: Short: target 400-600 words. One table or a handful of bullets, the US-domicile vs Irish UCITS trade-off, a conditional recommendation, an offer to expand. Must NOT produce a multi-section memo. Figures verified and date-stamped despite the brevity.

evals.name: rebalancing-no-contributions
evals.prompt: My equity sleeve has drifted up a fair bit after this year's run. Should I rebalance back to target, and how often should I be doing this generally?
evals.expected_output: Must recognise he has no regular contributions, so rebalancing means selling and realising gains. Should recommend wide tolerance bands, deploying irregular top-ups to the underweight sleeve, and selling only on a genuine band breach. Should explicitly reject calendar rebalancing. Must not recommend contribution-based rebalancing as though it were routinely available. No specific Brazilian tax rates.
